name.value: film-based emotion reactivity and regulation task

spans.text: film-based emotion reactivity and regulation task

description.value: Participants viewed positive, neutral, and negative film clips under watch or regulate instructions and rated their emotional responses.

spans.text: Participants viewed a series of forty 30‐second film clips that were either positive (e.g. babies laughing), neutral (e.g. weather report) or negative (e.g. documentary of the Rwandan genocide) in valence

stimuli.value: Forty 30-second positive, neutral, and negative film clips.

spans.text: Participants viewed a series of forty 30‐second film clips

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to watch the clips and allow emotions to arise naturally or to regulate negative affect using reappraisal.

spans.text: Either ‘watch’, where participants were told to watch the film clips and allow themselves to feel any emotions that naturally arose without trying to deliberately distract themselves from the content of the film clip or effortfully regulate their emotions in any way.

description.value: Participants watched negative 30-second film clips and were explicitly instructed to reduce their negative affect by using reappraisal to change how they thought about the film content; they then rated their emotional response from very negative (0) to very positive (10).

spans.text: Here, participants were explicitly asked to try to reduce (down-regulate) any negative affect in response to the film clip by using reappraisal techniques to change the way they thought about the contents of the film clip.
